channel.title: CT News Junkie - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from CT News Junkie (ctnewsjunkie.com)

item.title: The Supreme Court Struck Down Some Of Trump’s Tariffs, But Impact On CT Is Unclear, Experts Say
item.description: In a 6-3 ruling, the justices struck down about half of Trump’s tariffs, ruling that the law that he based them on does not grant the right to implement them. But what does that mean for Connecticut businesses and residents?

item.title: Eversource, UI Report Thousands Without Power In CT Due To Storm
item.description: Nearly 20,000 customers of the state's major utilities providers are without power Monday morning, according to information from Eversource and United Illuminating co.

item.title: Adams & Knight Welcomes New VP Of Media
item.description: After a long hiatus we have rebooted the 210 Capitol Ave blog to keep you filled in on the various news items in the industries adjacent to politics and public policy. It's been a while but we'll get you caught up.

item.title: CT Officials Report 80 Crashes, 70mph Winds As Storm Winds Down
item.description: Connecticut State Police reported about 250 calls for vehicle assistance, mostly vehicles off the road. There also were multiple jackknifed tractor trailers, according to Sgt. Mike Hamill, in addition to 82 traffic accidents resulting in a pair of minor injuries.

item.title: CT Bill Would Fund News Reporting Fellowships
item.description: The Connecticut General Assembly is considering a bill that would provide public funding for 12 early-career journalism fellowships in newsrooms around the state.

item.title: Supreme Court To Decide Key Issue In Fate Of State And City Suits Against Oil Companies Over Climate Change
item.description: From Baltimore to Honolulu, cities have made their views clear: Oil companies whose pollution contributed to climate change should be financially responsible for a fair share of the consequences.

item.title: Statehouse Partners Adds Pescatello To Team
item.description: Paul Pescatello, formerly senior counsel at the CBIA and executive director of the Connecticut Bioscience Growth Council, has joined Statehouse Partners as a lobbyist, according to the firm.

item.title: As CT Digs Out, More Snow Could Be On The Way
item.description: As Connecticut digs out from a major winter storm that dumped as much as two feet of snow in places, more snow could be coming in a series of storms later this week and early next week, according to early forecasts.

item.title: Energy Committee Hears From CT Officials On Aquarion Water Sale Bill
item.description: The bill, House Bill 7249, would affirm the legislature’s intent that PURA exercise review power over change in control of a water company. Backers hope to pass the legislation before PURA convenes again next month.

item.title: West Hartford Teen Succumbs to Injuries Sustained in Weekend Shooting
item.description: Hartford Police Lt. Aaron Boisvert said in a news release on Sunday that the shooting happened at approximately 1:49 a.m. on Feb. 22, in the vicinity of 181 Ann [Uccello] Street. That area is located just outside PeoplesBank Arena.
